667119e00128eea3.short: Emailed ahead and used a Guest of Honor certificate on a 137,000-point, 5-night stay. With low occupancy, many other guests got big upgrades too.

ef8d2d40aba0aa94.short: Gorgeous grounds, but the sargassum across the Riviera Maya brought an overwhelming sulfur smell. The lagoon pool reopened on arrival day, minus poolside service.

60d380b44244db34.short: Upgraded in advance to a suite of over 1,400 square feet, with huge deck-like balconies overlooking a Beringer reserve vineyard. Lived up to the hype.

6d686c3bab431d0a.short: Honeymoon room faced the noisy road. A staffer recorded them on a personal phone, and the GM only made good after corporate stepped in.

c4a0c992b89f32bd.short: Paid about $100 a night extra for the vineyard view. A good stay, though $1,000 in peak season felt hard to justify.

01b4844eb492e6c9.short: Nice room, bad spot right in front of valet check-in. Lunch came on arrival and departure days, the second as a packed hikers lunch.

184a31bd83fd695a.short: No suite and no resort credit, and that was fine. The one-entree-per-person rule covers in-room dinner orders too.

1a463b3c971916fc.short: S'mores came to the room, but paid cocktails replaced the free happy-hour drink. Lovely, yet hard to justify at roughly $2k a night in cash.

3e17fce4ca41db89.short: All meals included and excellent at Sur House, though room delivery costs $10. Liked the setting and food better than Post Ranch Inn.

44f7dcf5530089a3.short: Lovely sunsets and a quick text concierge, but poor pre-arrival contact and a $10 room-service delivery fee. Wonderful on points, not at $2k a night.

4676ef82310dccaf.short: Anniversary chocolates and champagne in a two-story villa. Bucket-list worthy as a redemption, less clear at the cash rate.

49f9bae326a8cab7.short: The suite sells for over $1,800, with a wood-burning fireplace and private patio hot tub. Breakfast was ordinary even with the $82 allowance.

4e03343b495f5403.short: The upgrade appeared in the app the day before arrival. Hammock and outdoor shower on the patio, plus a redwood picnic and s'mores.

6504da3ec55947a1.short: Room 56: near the hot baths with a sunset view, but facing the parking lot, so less privacy in the hot tub.

6b84e4efd10fe360.short: The anniversary upgrade was a surprise. The Cottage House is a standalone villa with a big private deck, hot tub and hammock.

70a9755fe3fc441f.short: Extra space on a Guest of Honor booking, close to the lobby and pool. Ground floor, though, with noise from guests and a dog above.

769619e09725f1aa.short: Worth the extra points for the Big Sur suite, not for the outdoor-shower version. So many Globalists on property that many went without upgrades.

780cb0df6ef918ba.short: Room 26 was scuffed and tired, the spa was full despite emails ahead, and service was very poor. Good food at Sur House.

7a688413bd2920e6.short: Would have traded the villa for a simpler one-level suite. Cheese and a half-bottle of wine on arrival, with upkeep and text replies much improved.

7f28070f6a8dd3a0.short: A two-story villa with the bedroom and open bathroom upstairs, plus surprise chocolates and champagne for the anniversary. Would definitely recommend.

7f321f0381df8ca0.short: Feels very exclusive at 50-60 rooms, all-inclusive except alcohol, with free valet and turndown gifts. Internet was very poor.

9a2ff31a353f9928.short: Great food, but confusing rules on what to order when, and the suite felt like a large junior suite. Keen to return for two nights.

a2347e6babea2045.short: No standard suite for the upgrade award, but check-in brought a Villa anyway. Meals ran on an $82 daily credit.

b771c238396668ab.short: Early check-in around noon on Valentine's weekend, and arrival-day lunch still came despite reports it was cut. Wonderful, worth the points and worth repeating.

bab095b6267fc84f.short: 4pm checkout, granted with a morning call. Social hour just okay, no welcome champagne, and an ordinary breakfast with $82 covered.

d00c097b1f281590.short: A mixed fourth visit: asked ahead to avoid Ridge House, yet got the same room there as two years earlier. Yellowjackets pushed dining indoors.

ddb2a6a4346f773d.short: A friend's Guest of Honor award, on a points stay with no Hyatt status. The Big Sur Suite was very nice.

ec3e8589c0388ba7.short: Canned lemonade, some moldy raspberries at breakfast and little made from scratch. Still a really nice stay, and probably a return.

ee0e7e80156adb96.short: The upgrade showed up in the app the day before the birthday trip, a kind gesture. Redwood view, a hammock and an outdoor shower.

16a392743dab8078.short: The front desk arranged the same suite for all six nights, even the first, which was on a category 1-7 free night certificate. Solid value.

1727e1d137dd6d44.short: $540 with tax for a narrow, minimalist box with a broken lighting panel. Rude service recovery, nice bathroom, and no plans to return.

44daeddc122552ce.short: The suite came once the hotel heard their son was flying in from Austin at the last minute. Their favorite Hyatt in New York.

70217f603d530ad2.short: A neighbor's noisy TV led to the move to the suite. Prosecco for the celebration, and in-room breakfast came off the bill.

b465af1ecced9e39.short: Red wine, chocolates and a call from the GM. An engineering issue forced the room move, handled flawlessly with apologies and points.

02983e17046b3bb9.short: An offer to pay got a free move to ocean view suite 618 the next day. Phenomenal whale watching from the balcony.

14ceacc364e91e31.short: All suites are renovated and the property is in good shape. Suite 140 felt private, and its bedroom lanai doesn't connect to the living-room one.

1673589b7bea5177.short: Two suites booked, side by side on the first floor. Snacks and champagne in both, plus marketplace cookies as the Globalist perk.

1a962203a69ebec0.short: Found the 850 sq ft suite upgrade in the app. Checkout went to 1pm, earlier than hoped, and their daughter got birthday cupcakes.

1f3e45f3341b5e70.short: A paid upgrade was $800 a night for the last three nights, too much. February was near perfect for weather and whale watching.

2149cc23a8bd1d3d.short: Both suites worn in Feb 2023: broken shades, damaged furniture. Not returning, mainly because management seemed dishonest about Globalist upgrades, and it's pricey.

2de9a8dd64bffaed.short: Room 138 faces trees, near stairs to the pool and beach. Moving to an Ocean suite was quoted at $200 a night, Deluxe Ocean $350.

4215023a4d2954db.short: Second stay, second time without a suite. Ripe fruit, rotating pastries and strong hot dishes at the buffet, with some waits this time.

53a9810ea902f1ad.short: The hotel was full, so seven nights in the booked room by the elevator. Still fantastic, and wrongly posted breakfast charges were fixed at checkout.

58bbdd5450a5cafa.short: Renovated and clearly better: new furniture, a quartz vanity, a glass shower in place of curtains. Occupancy seemed low after the Maui fires.

625300428151ebdf.short: The softer new pillow-top mattress did not suit their back. Breakfast is a buffet again, no a la carte, and lattes are $10 extra.

739bf4726e98ded7.short: Breakfast was good, not excellent, in July 2024. The roughly $9 machine cappuccino wasn't included, but the charge was dropped after a complaint about quality.

8357489cdaec01ae.short: No suite despite several asks, and when suites opened for the last three nights they were $800 a night. The room itself was flawless.

8d51c150c816cec6.short: Ground floor despite a flagged insect sensitivity. A move was $600, then $300 a night, until a big cockroach in the sink made it free.

c90a2ef1d0342a3e.short: Whales visible from the shower, and no resort fee charged. For a redeye, late checkout became a garden day-use room until 4pm.

cc2a6e8ea021446a.short: Told a suite certificate couldn't be used, then upgraded anyway to the best room yet here. Low occupancy and mostly broken EV chargers, but excellent.

d1a0387fbd8b8814.short: Told suites are no longer in the free upgrade pool. A 4pm checkout, refused at first, came through once the incoming guest was moved.

d2156d207b186c9e.short: Worth the $200 a night last year to move up to the Deluxe Ocean Suite. The base suite faced a wall.

d65b294e9502f0ba.short: Told a standard suite can't be upgraded for Globalists anymore, and the paid offer got its inclusions wrong. Unimpressed so far.

ddddf7e5a4533109.short: A December week with generally good recognition. The renovation is holding up well, and weekend breakfast gets busy but stays manageable.

e5a5fde541022a7e.short: Upgrades here seem to stop at a basic ocean room. Excellent, uncrowded breakfast with good papaya and pineapple, and juice cocktails are back.

f0d20a7be4c33d2f.short: With the hotel full, even a paid ocean-view move ($150-$200 a night) wasn't possible until night three. Loved the relaxed vibe and cove snorkeling.

fca96ac34390fa43.short: The hotel emailed ahead and put them in a partial-view room on the fifth floor. A birthday mention brought generous in-room treats.

fd2e1efd8077dbcf.short: Asked about a further upgrade the day before. Check-in offered only a paid ocean-view suite at $300 a night, yet five suites were bookable online.

ff21978a5f23df00.short: Suite award applied by hand through the Globalist line, with parking and resort fees waived. Stingy with further upgrades, but no hard feelings.

194103363f9c4d21.short: Upgrades are hit or miss, and Miami Suites usually lack balconies. No longer aspirational, just a decent beach resort.

1b56099826d82154.short: Took a Miami Suite ready at 10am, then switched to the oceanfront one around 12:30. Great value on category 4 certificates.

3c1cbe5ed2e14fce.short: Worn room and hallway, like a beachy Waikiki apartment, plus noise from the next building's fan. Public spaces were decently nice.

65e5b49761bd3d2e.short: Picked the 10th-floor ocean view over a 4th-floor Miami suite. Free valet, but kelp on the beach and fewer places to eat than farther south.

d92ee300aa6e0622.short: Kept the suite for a fifth points night. Noon checkout since it was sold out, plus a room offered for their son's afternoon nap.

4cf3e5ec62822e4a.short: Breakfast covered for the whole family, plated at the Globalist-only Ostra or the main buffet. Andaz hats and flip-flops in the room.

9300490ab5c9a8b3.short: Upgraded on the one Chase certificate night and kept the suite all five nights. Monkeys in the trees, no HVAC in the bathrooms.

9ca5ca6ef4cc5c4d.short: Possibly the best breakfast outside Asia and the Middle East. Weak shower pressure and hit-and-miss service, but strongly recommended, especially with a suite upgrade.

b24136a07c742601.short: Minibar beers were free according to staff, but the hotel would not drop the charges. Still rated the resort highly overall.

e7c59da0a1b351c0.short: Upgraded at check-in, with suites sold out on this 2021 anniversary trip. Matching hats and flip-flops were left in the room.

16b4644e5c0ca961.short: Picked to fit 2 adults and teens. Huge, with a daybed the size of two twins, and the manager waived the planned mid-stay move.

58fd077a164a86c8.short: Would pick the Andaz over the Conrad Singapore even at 50% more. Much nicer rooms, a separate WC, a far better breakfast if less varied.

60d879e9eea2e1f3.short: The suite sits under the steakhouse, so bar music came through the wood floor past its 10:30pm close. Took about 35 minutes to sort out.

78a95ec38092a2e7.short: Asked for a Deluxe Sea View and heard Heritage View was already a double upgrade, though the website puts it one category up. Felt misled.

e0b2ee90a3ddad0d.short: Service was excellent, which in their experience is rare in Singapore, and the doorman knew their name. Oddly shaped suite with too-clever light switches.

1f8560ca29e78613.short: A dinner service issue ended with the whole meal comped. Charcuterie on arrival, an electric fireplace in the bedroom, and 2pm checkout.

58c44a64c4bac2ad.short: A March stay, extended until the Covid closure, with better treatment than at Highlands Inn. Only gripe: lots of kids at events.

b54752d4199d9c34.short: Probably the last visit, now that it costs the same points as Ventana. Upgrade refused outright, and the salmon came undercooked.

bba4cd9933c1312c.short: The Ranch Suite was worth about $1k, but a further bump was declined with premium suites showing open. Cookies and fruit waiting, and 3pm checkout.

c557d19b976f797c.short: Moved to the suite after ants turned up in the first room. Room-service and to-go breakfasts cost extra, and Valley Kitchen felt slow.

efb80e89189dadcc.short: A notch below Ventana on hardware, ahead of it on staff recognition. Wine in the room and 2pm checkout.

f2fd36c328e65501.short: Preferred to Alila Ventana Big Sur in the offseason for the reasonable cash rates. Loved the activities and already booked a return trip.

fcb3e1f9499348ed.short: Second stay, cut short when a nearby fire and an evacuation warning shut the property down. Shorter breakfast menu, many activities suspended.

2516ecb408f2d4ce.short: Suite upgrade awards can't be used here. Destination fees waived, and while the suite was more a big room, loved the furniture and tub.

66dd6c262b98eb2f.short: Upgraded in the app. Founders Suites were in use for a photo shoot, but a longtime staffer showed off the architectural details.

717632b6a748d1f7.short: Three nights in two rooms, both small and gloomy, with very bad WiFi. Superb location, but won't book again because of the dark rooms.

a83722ab1f7e3828.short: No recognition at check-in, El noise, and folio errors on tips and parking. Only the Cherry Circle Room breakfast was outstanding.

b70791602b9572fb.short: Turned down for a corner view room with suites still selling. The Founders Fee waiver took a reminder, and the welcome drink was embarrassingly tiny.

e4c2c9c2a51b3b71.short: One of only three Founders Suites, with a big gas fireplace. Great recognition at check-in, awesome breakfast, excellent bars and restaurants.

11e88a888aa86d96.short: No recognition at check-in, but the buffet was among the best of any American hotel. The bill briefly read nearly $2,700, then $13 once fixed.

22bd1d591232d35e.short: Felt understaffed: no housekeeping until 4pm each day, no ski valet rack by the chairlift, no kids club. A $250 credit was offered after complaints.

b5fd6fa6b1e306d0.short: Breakfast was a $30 daily credit per person, enough for most entrees plus coffee, tip and tax. Gift of chocolate truffles and Oregon red wine.

ce195e9ea874f578.short: Upgraded from a room under $300 a night though the hotel had shown sold out. Awesome valley view and heated pool, but breakfast needs work.

4db0143753819f3a.short: Terrific at 15k a night against low expectations. Warmer than the Park Hyatt New York suite at 30k a night the weekend before.

7bc2b3464f091cc1.short: A certificate night when most Manhattan hotels were $400-500, plus a 2,000-point Brand Explorer bonus. Big for NYC, very high ceilings, but dim by day.

81e914259ea213a8.short: A 6:30am check-in after a redeye. The retro-elegant room felt fresh, not dated, but ran cold on winter nights in the poorly insulated old building.

8992eb680ffe6742.short: The best points deal in Manhattan, with a $100 breakfast limit and chatty staff. The Gold Street entrance can be tricky to find by car.

9b134964d66fea2e.short: Decor felt like a done-up Hyatt Place, not boutique luxury. A low-floor suite despite booking early, and two bathrooms felt like wasted space.

a3a4dc4863fa4609.short: Told King suites were sold out, apparently untrue, and a manager apologized with a free glass of prosecco. Small room, noisy HVAC, but would return.

b19c6c52b04f925a.short: Roomy for NYC, but the full bath sits by the front door, far from the bedroom. Heaters struggled in the cold, thermostats mostly for show.

2eef8caafa559733.short: The night after opening, no late checkout was offered and breakfast went unexplained. Liked the friendly staff, gym, Grand Club design and AirTrain link.

462c978e406fb47f.short: The front desk texted ahead about arrival and departure times, a nice touch and a first. A suite request worked, with a slightly later arrival.

948021545e5315d1.short: No suite, but a solid room with bay and airport views, and a good restaurant breakfast. Valet-only parking was a small annoyance.

9bd5f06d0b658218.short: A late one-night booking still got a corner suite, though none showed as available. Their vote for best Hyatt elite treatment in the US.

dbf146b71838bc10.short: Only eight hours, with drinks and snacks in the Grand Lounge before bed. Elite upgrades here get good marks from other Globalists in the thread.

19bfda728dae2639.short: Suite award arranged through a concierge, and the suite was like two rooms joined. Housekeeping and toiletry slips made it a mixed stay.

45574df31f0730b7.short: An email before arrival warned upgrades were limited, yet one came at check-in. Downsides were three wrong room charges and uneven buffet service.

5849884b5f919373.short: The upgrade came from Globalist status, not the Prive booking, per staff. Unobstructed water view, and resort fees waived at checkout.

896040cd48af99b5.short: A mother-daughter trip on free nights, with Bahamian candies as the gift. The Regatta buffet breakfast and nightly drink vouchers were the best perks.

b828c4f3ddbd4e11.short: Suite award, then a further move up to a residence with a washer/dryer, full kitchen and big living room. Excellent buffet and service.

c0c6014ae9c0dcba.short: A shower leak flooded the Grand Suite's bedroom, and staff sent people to check twice before a reluctant move. Still a great trip.

dc9ecf98b6fb8592.short: Two rooms, suite award on one. Breakfast for two per room, valet parking and daily drink vouchers, plus good service and status recognition.

e4e4fd9a42d5064e.short: A suite with two balconies, worth about $300 a night more than the standard room. 1pm checkout on request, and resort fees waived.

e4ec55591aaa3b54.short: Upgraded before arrival, then moved into the Reserve, with a small VIP lounge. Swamped at peak times, but friendly staff and very good food.

2d06ac9c1d35c2b9.short: Two nights for 36,000 points, with breakfast in the Grand Club and at Vox.

81d9e5e2a4b42cdb.short: A poor view in the standard suite, so asked to move. Switching to two queens got a bigger specialty suite, a huge improvement.

dae60f6a07248d59.short: The club's evening dinner buffet beat the main breakfast restaurant. The front desk handled a complex multi-room points-and-cash booking well.

02214c3e9bdaee49.short: The kids' twin room also went up to a harbor view on the same floor. Outstanding service, and Grand Club visits at least twice daily.

58f925135443885c.short: No corner deluxe or suite on a New Year's Eve staycation, a first in about twenty stays. Still good, and the lounge crew was great.

9f4017473e19d714.short: Christmas stay booked on a mix of cash and a category-7 certificate. Checked in at 8am.

b579f5c7919e0a28.short: Suite award guaranteed for all four nights, three on points and one on a free-night certificate. Gift of wine, pistachios and refilled fruit.

ce93d114f8371aa5.short: Club-level room first, then a call a few hours later to move to a suite. Checkout stopped at 4pm, but a spare room was offered.

f9d672e65be934b1.short: Harbor view for the week, and a welcome gift of wine, macaroons, pistachios, chocolates, a refilled fruit platter and a coffee machine. Wonderful club staff.

0b6767917a2911ae.short: Suite award refused until Hyatt customer service stepped in, and the pools were insanely crowded over Labor Day. Fine suite, but would not return.

25bbc12d5a01c954.short: September 2021 workcation in one of 26 top-floor suites. Housekeeping skipped several days after a busy weekend, but the room and halls were extremely quiet.

5f78a11b313e9bea.short: A pre-arrival email ruled out suite upgrades due to heavy occupancy. Asking if that applied to Globalists got the Penthouse suite, but check-in was robotic.

672976b4e5af4b87.short: Heard about the villa by text the morning of check-in. Room ready at 1pm, but nobody explained perks and late checkout took a separate ask.

c022c6bc6c3ce49b.short: Turned down non-connecting suites or a one-bedroom villa to keep the kids' rooms connected. In at 11am, out at 2pm, with great grounds and pools.

24e5a1a2188d9f0b.short: A surprise suite upgrade showed up in the app. Booked suites come with breakfast and club access at any status, but this upgrade did not.

286a8b1f1f5bd201.short: 1,636 square feet, with a living room, dining room, guest bath and walk-in closet. Club staff made clear not to expect it every time.

6b0b6699f8a47043.short: Six nights, with the Petronas Twin Towers view added on arrival. The Grand Club team arranged a birthday cake for a friend.

bff02074fa0ae60e.short: The 1,500-square-foot suite came on a second visit within ten days. A lounge staffer even fetched a forgotten knife unprompted.

c6e8958d688f183c.short: The executive lounge was closed for weekday breakfast with no warning, and housekeeping missed a day and was late with turndown. Would not return.

e5a117a305757552.short: Checked in at the Grand Club around 12:30pm. Late checkout was 6pm, past the standard 4pm.

0ac6282b1e07d1fc.short: The deluxe king matched the grand suite in size. Enjoyed the pool, spa and club's free-pour spirits, though happy hour was crowded.

48e8552439c8ad3a.short: In at 7:45am for a one-night points stay on a long layover. Good service, but the furnishings felt dated.

7be22e94a6ed8919.short: Robotic check-in with no nod to status. Club lounge staff and evening offerings were good, and restaurant breakfast was included.

198c46d478418518.short: Slightly preferred to the Centric, with a better breakfast. Resort fee removed, small room with no mini-fridge, and now on the will-return list.

99f59f403f37ec6b.short: One $220 night with 4pm checkout. Digital key failed, pillows far too firm, squirt-gun shower, but solid breakfast and a comfy modern room.

a456f1a0bc746435.short: Staff seemed reluctant to upgrade at first. A noisy connecting door, a bathroom window facing the bed, no balcony furniture, yet would stay again.

01ca2b3c89138168.short: Not offered a bungalow at first, though one showed open on arrival day. Old bathrooms, good Hana Ranch breakfast, but Category 7 felt too rich.

1f5f56dc7fbe5e3e.short: A December storm left the wifi too slow for remote work, and food trucks were the best food when open. Planning five days next time.

3c6b06ed84571d29.short: A true ocean-front suite with an oversized lanai and four lounge chairs. Breakfast was good, and so was the Thai food truck.

5ef5f83304b630fb.short: Biggest letdown of the trip for the price. The room bottomed out at 77.5 degrees with 72% humidity, and the bed was awful.

6593ac34bd5fb8b8.short: Full rate, and the view was mostly the bungalow below. The hotel had no record of an April stay, and management never responded.

757a2c3e7e6eae97.short: A perfect end to Maui after a hectic week in Wailea. Pick the three-digit ocean-view bungalows across the road over the two-digit garden-view ones.

554604c5912852f2.short: Upgraded a few days ahead, and a separate three-night stay got a Junior Suite with view. Suite upgrade awards aren't accepted, freeing suites for elites.

5841c72b357c425c.short: Pitched a 150 EUR-a-night junior suite, offered an ADA room, then no room for hours. Effectively a downgrade, though the hotel was not sold out.

730d675bef632857.short: A 100% upgrade rate, from a deluxe king with view to the Palais Royal Suite. Mostly one- or two-night stays, though.

7e10530a6fd2ed66.short: Central but too touristy, like Times Square. Breakfast service was pleasant, the selection underwhelming, and the Hyatt Paris Madeleine would be the pick instead.

417ae30aabb6c169.short: The go-to downtown LA pick over the InterContinental, for value and suite upgrades when available. Parking nearby cost a quarter of the hotel's valet.

5a752be0d5ec70ad.short: Unbeatable value at under $200 a night for a suite. The layout was bigger than recent photos show, with windows in bedroom and living room.

73baeaac337fc124.short: A relief to be moved out of the 1-queen room, and the welcome gift was striking.

d3423c7c3b7cfd58.short: No nod as a returning guest, and mixed answers on whether the breakfast voucher covered coffee and juice. A little less generous than before.

e6e70f9516c178f7.short: Booked the suite for just $5 more than a standard room, valet included. Friends in a second room got breakfast and late checkout too, unasked.

bad76a452a66f7a7.short: Applied the suite award just one to two weeks out. The $26.50 per-person credit worked at the restaurant and market pantry, and they'd gladly return.

d88af11959469fbb.short: With the governor suite unavailable, the front desk manager showed them the presidential suite and later upgraded the father's room for two nights free.

e3662c3374a7a231.short: Grilled by the front desk over a key problem. At 5am every sound came through the adjoining room's wall, and breakfast service felt hostile.

fd60471bc6d2b062.short: Both stays brought a corner suite with floor-to-ceiling windows. Amazing food on the $26.50 credit, free valet, and a better vibe than the Grand Hyatt.

3148ba78e75ad9ae.short: With the restaurant open again, order off the menu rather than the buffet. Rooms facing the hospital can mean broken sleep from sirens.

357a3354e1b8b918.short: Two award nights in late November 2020. Restaurant and bar closed for COVID, and the room had been disinfected and left empty for 24 hours.

37a1fa307e725506.short: Best hotel buffet since COVID began, plus free parking on an award stay. Ambulances from the hospital next door were loud overnight.

554d0d997f24c584.short: Excellent Globalist treatment for a Centric, perks explained at check-in. Odd bathroom layout, fast breakfast, and would make it the Chicago default.

6947fd479ed0f821.short: Around $80 a night, with wine and chocolate cake for the birthday. Huge, flavorless breakfast portions, but still the favorite Hyatt in Chicago.

97cd668a4a12ab0f.short: A very large room looking out at the St. Regis and Trump Tower. The $15 restaurant credit seemed to come with the destination fee.

beac6ffdbdd4859c.short: A minimal upgrade didn't matter with the parents in an executive suite. Kind staff, tasty breakfast, unbeatable location: would stay again.

d4b4990bc6b36965.short: Moved over from a nearby DoubleTree in November 2017. Friendly desk, a new, quiet corner room with a plain view, good food and poor coffee.

da7b5931e243ef8e.short: Breakfast off the menu every day: high-quality dishes, unusual options and great fresh juices. Good gym, good staff, a very nice four days.

f81ec6977e0f63ff.short: No bar or breakfast yet in March 2021, so the hotel paid 500 points a day. Mostly deserted, with a very good gym.

10203d4c94e3ff6d.short: Quiet and comfortable for a family of four, and the only gripe was staff who couldn't answer basic transit questions. Would go back.

19e0827b5bb2ea98.short: A $104 advance-purchase status run with the destination fee waived, and a pretty good breakfast for two at about $50. Good value.

d7dde2cfab0c1a2b.short: Avoid front-facing rooms at all costs. The upgraded room was horribly noisy day and night, the worst noise ever for a Manhattan local.

fa731e1ed5f22340.short: The courtyard room didn't look like even the best available, though the hotel was sold out. The $20 destination fee wasn't brought up at check-in.

0cced76b9b0d6e57.short: A note asking for a king got nowhere. Two free bar drinks, but next time it's elsewhere unless the stay credit is needed.

af5f39e559b4dff3.short: Rebooked at 15k points a night when a suite opened about four days out. Small and quiet, with a sewage smell a few nights.

ef02590342cfbd88.short: With the restaurant closed, the hotel handed out two $15 gift cards for Roanoke around the corner. Missed breakfast, which was pulled at 9am.

32b54fc6e6c5429e.short: With Farmhouse closed for refurbishment, breakfast moved to Cruise as a semi-buffet. Some of the same chefs, much the same food, maybe even better.

9e9b575050fb7034.short: Elites can check in at the 22nd-floor Victoria Lounge, skipping the crowded lobby. The west tower has direct street access, and the east does not.

cdcd11f693fe11c0.short: One Duck Lane, the new buffet in the old Farmhouse space, has slow service and waits. Liked Cruise's made-to-order better, but still coming back.

e4c2e8aa7af2f81b.short: Skyline views from the harbor-front promenade right outside, in an area nicer than Wan Chai or Tsim Sha Tsui. Second favorite of the Hyatts tried.

7d9b3fc26b801c73.short: The suite upgrade cleared at mobile check-in, then the front desk gave a base room with deluxe rooms open. One key, musty smell, no toiletries.

bf8ec4f87247f518.short: Spacious rooms, mediocre service. Poor soundproofing let in footsteps on the same floor and sirens, though the area is quiet most of the day.

0495c1cabf5a1458.short: Bigger than the Andaz kings, with a modern bathroom. Much better value than pricier Hyatts nearby, though they wouldn't spend category-6 points on it.

d2e75982a5f76dee.short: Felt much smaller than the corner suite shown online, with a tiny bathroom and no real workspace. Would avoid the hotel unless location is key.

d601d0f35d0ac3f2.short: A disgrace for a paid suite: a closet-sized bathroom, ugly furniture, trash in the halls and unsecured elevators. Would never stay again.

e6380ca7f764b4f4.short: The 9,000-point upgrade gave a suite that worked for a family with kids. Removing breakfast charges took a manager at checkout.

c32c798488f76f9b.short: One of the best Hyatt breakfasts in a long time, but claustrophobic rooms, sloppy renovation and a tiny gym. Moved to the Andaz 5th Avenue.

f212cad6d3855252.short: The deluxe king upgrade was just a higher floor, a $10-a-night difference, with suites for sale. Tiny, no desk, but surprisingly quiet.

fdee6c8f3af9b97a.short: Far bigger than the 224-square-foot King Suite listed online, with Empire State Building views. The best Hyatt suite yet.

2f074c2492d40eee.short: 12,000 points a night. Free, easy street parking and a nightly beer-and-wine reception, but a slow-draining shower was never fixed.

37fe608aa33b718b.short: Living room, dining table and a balcony facing the pool and mountains, plus four drink coupons at check-in. Pink marble bathrooms, dated but working.

cc7f00a64a03f9ab.short: Not worth the suite award, just a standard room with a view. Expired cheese in the amenity, good pool and fire pits, no charm.

404867572968c168.short: A choice of suites for five nights working from the hotel, plus 4pm checkout. Some noise from the pool below was the only drawback.

7bcb36eab1553153.short: Very good Regency Club: snacks from noon, hearty evening food with free beer and wine. Incredible service, two to three staff always on hand.

7f76c3c131937664.short: The Regency Club has views, seating inside and out, and beer and wine in the evening. Tasty breakfast buffet, solid hors d'oeuvres.

aee516a509bbbf92.short: Only a modest bump with the hotel 30% full, and late checkout just to noon. Still a great trip, and would likely return.

d681c82f46ff4b03.short: Globalist breakfast is only at the Palms, a buffet with eggs and omelets made to order. Specialty coffee costs extra.

dee850674888d80c.short: Asking to switch got a much bigger end-of-hall room with a full balcony. Stingy with upgrades at very low occupancy, but relaxed and uncrowded.

5f6a381924bbf9d7.short: A week on floor 21 with very good staff, service and food. A second booking later that month could not get a suite.

73751deaa772cb6b.short: No line into the lounge around 5:30pm. Some guests' manners were poor, but staff stayed calm and kind.

857e80d7668ce98e.short: Long club lines at cocktail hour, hall noise through a thin suite door, and noon checkout for the suite only. No plans to return.

bc0e6591cafc112b.short: A fantastic use of the award for a week. 4pm checkout meant switching rooms around midday, and the low floor got street noise.

c3c30c746b74f156.short: Would have preferred a king deluxe. Great hotel and fantastic breakfast, but rates are out of hand and the area is not for families.

eae08d2020e22210.short: Seedy street scene, but it did not matter. Good breakfast, a nice lounge with outdoor seating, a fine pool and good value.

f644350871df2df1.short: Best use of Hyatt points in Bangkok, with a direct link to Nana BTS. The club's evening spread is enough for dinner.

4d07ec8544ab6eb5.short: Nearly a week over Thanksgiving, in adjoining suites with wide pool and lake views. Check-in brought champagne and a resort-fee discount.

8676a13ea30f815b.short: A lounge among the US's best, good Hyatt Camp for the kid. Chilly pools, very slow room service, rowdy guests, but would stay again.

10cc0d5403aff6c3.short: About $190 all-in on a 10% corporate rate for a comfortable but dated, worn suite. The amenity was a coupon for one provisions-shop item.

31f0a94a4a4b47e1.short: Ten nights at 25k points a night over New Year's, with free valet and a s'mores package. Asking got only a deluxe king, no cottage.

96225cde8181e0cf.short: An email to the GM's office got a renovated tower room with a bay window. A housekeeping slip brought a $50 credit.

a7549618c5b202e2.short: Paid resort and parking fees at this tier, and a 2pm checkout request became 1pm after asking again that morning. High-quality buffet, crowded beach.

035645a36e0f451b.short: Shell leis on arrival and a 4pm late checkout on request. Their daughter's birthday brought a snack basket and a towel cake.

3a60467ad76b30f9.short: A letdown for a yearly regular: staff cuts at Japengo, no egg station, a thin club, pushy timeshare pitches all week. The GM sent cupcakes.

f2453c1bd19673e3.short: Seven nights in two rooms for the family at 25k points per night, a very good use of points. Staff were very friendly.

067daf9e7484f038.short: On a one-night layover with kids, the VIP manager handled the bags and gave the children Eiffel Tower keychains. A comfortable first night in Paris.

7cd00b7e3b75a472.short: Newly renovated, with simple, stylish rooms and views of the Eiffel Tower and Arc de Triomphe. A modern high-rise, not quaint Paris.

df594211e4acdfa5.short: Jackhammers, slow elevators and cramped rooms amid renovation, though the breakfast buffet was good. Late checkout was refused by phone, then grudgingly given until 2pm.

17d80daac472dd65.short: Spent a 14-day COVID quarantine here in October 2020, better value than the Fairmont. Breakfast bags at the door, healthier on request.

255da704e42f30ba.short: Good, not great, with free parking and a good but limited Mosaic buffet. Only worth it as a Globalist on points, given the high rates.

58d5258b3dedabc6.short: Two suite upgrades in roughly 7 to 10 stays, both connecting rooms with two full baths. Main gripe: tubs only, no walk-in showers.

6dbcf1ab40ae8989.short: Disappointing that Globalist breakfast is in the new lounge instead of the restaurant. The lounge is pleasant, with OK food and friendly staff.

b2bf4ebf028d42b8.short: Warned ahead that suites were out for renovation. Comfortable bed, skyline views, an omelet station and smoked salmon at breakfast, and 4pm checkout.

d79463bf1bf79b01.short: Globalist breakfast moved to the 34th-floor English Bay Room during the restaurant's renovation. Much the same spread as before, with better views.

79928639c5a39e91.short: One of the better Globalist breakfasts in the city, and only the steak and eggs cost extra. Very happy despite a small Manhattan room.

a6f50e7bea34cc69.short: Six-night mattress run. A leaking window meant a suite for the final night, and a $20 chit replaced the welcome bubbles.

350afa4b5eb10b93.short: A $199 night in a small but comfortable room, fine for one. Two local beers, the destination fee dropped without question, and genuinely friendly staff.

5ab248931deabf65.short: A welcome-back note and two cocktails in the fridge. When breakfast codes came late one morning, the desk phoned right away with 5,000 points.

5b0829204a97a464.short: Same room as last time and two free beers at check-in. Great shakshuka next door on the emailed vouchers, but some housekeeping misses.

944d808a23b1436b.short: Talked out of the bigger studio over noise. Room not ready until 4pm but spotless, with a Canal Street view, plus a free Chinatown tour.

f9231ec304032522.short: An apology call from the assistant director of rooms when the suite wasn't ready, plus a personal email from the GM. Would definitely return.

bd983b8436189eed.short: Peekaboo Golden Gate Bridge views and a good blend of modern and Japanese design. Mall parking, $29 a night, is cheap for San Francisco.

e6d29f0b11ebdce1.short: Offered a high floor or a suite at check-in, and valet was free with no argument. If only more Hyatts were like this.

2f28673a1bbc095b.short: A 2018 stay, soon after the hotel joined Marriott. The welcome gift has since dropped from a macaron and chocolate box to a fruit bowl.

86eb827363fd599e.short: Only lounge access until asking about upgrades as a Titanium with over 1,800 nights. Got a 4pm checkout unasked and took the 1,000 points.

bdc4c7a89a81ebb3.short: Restaurant breakfast at Beach Road Kitchen is back for elites, a recent improvement. The welcome amenity was 1,000 points.

c326549fbed168a7.short: Eight awards saved over two years cleared for the late-August stay, a week after a nearby Marriott failed to clear one. Macarons and chocolates too.

d1e54d874a9023f4.short: One of Southeast Asia's best lounges that year, with made-to-order cocktails, plus a TWG tea set. Would stay regularly if the company budget allowed.

47d4916b4c1d9778.short: No Suite Night Award allowed, but the upgrade came the morning before check-in. Corsair's buffet was mediocre and skipped on later days.

f1858b63e40e1295.short: Loved the Lamarck suite despite a dim, TV-less living room. Great architecture, decor and friendly staff, and so fantastic overall they booked a return.

2d4df20f0008d795.short: Saw the sunset upgrade in the app a few days out. Paid $150 a night plus taxes at check-in to add a pool, highly recommended.

806b1dd69a131e45.short: All-inclusive was better value than half board, with the Japanese restaurant and drinks anywhere. Checkout around 2pm for the last seaplane.

c251d6171a418f64.short: The sunrise villa felt better than a sunset one, and the steaks at Turquoise and Velaa were great. Tops other mid-to-high-end hotels they've tried.

4ee46a6bb657f30b.short: Classy and well kept. Without the points to earn, though, a Premier Inn in the same building would feel similar for much less.

9595acc3fc7253f0.short: Over Christmas to New Year 2018, the balcony views were wonderful despite scaffolding on the clock tower. A Thames-side location and decent elite recognition.

b9f53964ff386840.short: Generous lounge food and pours, but a stuffy room with weak AC and uncomfortable beds. Won't return at over 500 pounds a night.

bb224206e5300f6e.short: Sparkling wine at check-in, a 4pm checkout on request, London map wallpaper, a great shower and good lounge table service. Would come back.

e9d44724a314c479.short: Full hotel, so no Big Ben or Thames view, but among the largest big-city base rooms they had seen. Will return despite unreliable WiFi.

27fc6f020d4fc943.short: Breakfast, confusing at first, was comped at $24 a person for four, but the cafe opened at 8am and was slammed. Great location, would return.

8eab34eb05e30746.short: Splendid ocean views and one of the nicest room-service breakfasts in a while. Fabulous weekday rate, $10-a-day parking, friendly staff.

952f8a149dbb6858.short: Modest upgrade in a sold-out week, garage parking waived for EV charging. Loved the spot across from the beach, though the pool was crowded.

fe1a39bb48efeb4c.short: One night at $134 during construction, the front desk in the workout room. Still problem-free, with a fabulous breakfast and smooth checkout.

fefa9a7e20fe5e07.short: A go-to in Santa Barbara, and the balcony was the best part. Costa breakfast covered an entree, fruit and a latte daily.

f81e329143235d2a.short: Shabby, motel-like open-air corridors, but almost everything else was perfect: 850 square feet, two balconies, manta rays nightly. Preferred to a Maldives resort.

d67fe24cd453c206.short: A $40 daily food credit per person, good at the restaurants or room service. Huge, fast-filling tub, weak sink pressure, and lots of families.

dda5deae503f0697.short: Pre-arrival emails and texts, a personal follow-up from the guest services manager, and the Christmas buffet brunch comped as breakfast. Can't wait to return.

347ada3d9a2f5550.short: A suite in name only. Toiletries then were small bottles of The White Company Sandalwood, not big pump bottles of Acqua di Parma.

5dff588298cf2e0e.short: A whole trip built around the suite upgrade award, about 15 months back. Fantastic and highly recommended, with an excellent location and a wonderful lobby.

6adb27715d5a43ba.short: Very large but one big room, no privacy, and street noise went unnoticed at night with windows closed in winter. Loved the photogenic lobby.

dc337e5d6970a885.short: Chosen for the light and bathroom windows. A patio door off the bathroom was too exposed to the busy intersection to use.

5508a804521ff430.short: First-ever suite upgrade in Asia, through the app. Very roomy but dated, mostly facing other buildings, with a massive tub and free cookies.

88266925375ca168.short: Great sauna, service and value. Beats the nearby Paradise 9 times out of 10, though breakfast trails Park Hyatt Seoul a smidge.

bbe1d75c136af340.short: Told upgrades stop at a certain floor, though higher ones had rooms open and a standard suite was still for sale. Globalist upgrades capped?

13eca91876e52537.short: Ordered over the $48 breakfast cap cited before, and it was all waived. Service noticeably better and more professional than last time.

1bc39aa87725be66.short: Told there were no upgrades, then moved up on check-in day. Among the city's best luxury hotels, though an ice request sat for hours.

4acc4084460837ed.short: Keys ready with no wait after a redeye, not what they expect from Hyatt. Excellent service, communication and hard product.

5d9327f436522847.short: Water Tower and lake views from the new suite, and breakfast excellent again. A wonderful hotel with extremely friendly, professional staff.

a2d2dea2a4a7b141.short: Largest suite award result ever with Hyatt, two bathrooms with Toto bidets. Quiet for a light sleeper, great breakfast apart from one overcooked steak.

ae908732a1e17dc4.short: Surprisingly disappointing service on a return stay. Room not ready, and the stored bags never came up as promised, so they fetched them themselves.

c8b1c5e19de19538.short: An excellent couple of nights, with helpful, friendly staff and strong breakfast choices. Will definitely come back on future Chicago trips.

e6c32c7b4e1f6afd.short: A modest city view upgrade seemed fair for a busy concert weekend. Now weighing a Water Tower or lake view deluxe room.

f3b15e7a2dcf5903.short: Breakfast now means one entree, one hot drink, one cold drink, no cap. Steak and eggs, coffee and a smoothie, about $85, all waived.

7375be797121ca73.short: Baklava as the welcome gift, truffle eggs and Arabic options at breakfast, and checkout at 4pm. Quiet on a Sunday night, with a strong shower.

88fb4dd106589b86.short: The confirmed suite was pulled the day before arrival when its occupant stayed on. The returned award was expiring, so of no use.

f2c7f1b65a5ce34f.short: When a bellhop damaged camera gear, management replaced the lens hood, took costs off the bill and offered 15,000 points. Normally a $755-a-night suite.

07f055c73da6a7da.short: Five nights over Gion Matsuri in a Park Suite with a big private garden. Excellent service, but the Japanese breakfast surcharge was poor value.

21293462b1f20107.short: Booked on points at the last minute. The room came with a private zen garden, and a fruit basket was waiting.

2f84dfc5c1aa29d6.short: Service and design were thoroughly impressive. The corner suite faces the street, though, and people walking by can see in.

79c8ee2fad7d0424.short: Service was extraordinary, from seated check-in and champagne to a tour from the manager. Two sharing one king bed needed a rollaway.

89230017d544aac1.short: Birthday stay: two categories up, a private Japanese garden, a cake and a tote bag. Suite upgrades are rare here.

981dde51feb9e653.short: Treated well, with a Yasaka pagoda view and the champagne happy hour. Early-morning temple visits were a favorite.

9cc7c30c54121be4.short: Booked one of the hotel's two Park Suites for three nights at peak autumn foliage. The hotel was nearly full, so no further upgrade.

a212d17ec65362a9.short: One award night at the New Year hatsumode peak. Arrival service was underwhelming, with little info on breakfast.

a5e7e210e05428c5.short: Arrived around midnight, with 2pm late checkout on that first room. Next morning, after a smaller view room was offered, got the last Park Suite.

b1f917dde6dcfdea.short: Don't count on an upgrade at any Hyatt tier in this 70-room hotel: neither room got one. The 45 sqm room was spacious and calm.

c07099551abd934d.short: No king swap for the twin booking. Kyoto Bistro breakfast was the buffet plus one menu dish, and the Japanese set cost extra.

e23679dd62f5e535.short: Picked the Garden Terrace from two upgrade choices offered at check-in. Suite awards were no use, with no standard suites open.

87b0c28eb4e5bf15.short: Almost no drawer space, low hot-water pressure, and a lockless terrace door that blew open. Fantastic Park Lounge with great gluten-free service.

e356de4884009a19.short: Junior-suite sized, with a fireplace and a bathroom nearly as big as the room. Loved the CBD views and service, and would definitely return.

e5b4025f84bbc0f5.short: Dated and tired, with an $8 upcharge for hot breakfast items that should be free and a poorly stocked lounge. Mediocre for a Park Hyatt.

4bd5bd299375a971.short: A beautiful hotel with free room-service breakfast each morning. Several plain-looking suites count as premium, so suite awards can't touch them.

544f010abf14fd7f.short: The $720 Prive night came with the upgrade, but keeping the room for the 35,000-point night cost $50. Warm service, breakfast only okay.

63f79df5c7120800.short: Top-notch, with classy, prompt service and Le Labo now in big wall-mounted bottles. Room-service breakfast for two ran $150 to $190, all wiped.

682f64757413eb59.short: Keeping the suite past night one: $250, then $300 a night, which felt like a used-car-salesman shakedown. The manager later apologized and comped it.

6ad50b2ffdfa94ca.short: The suite came as a one-time courtesy, with 4pm checkout. Busy checkout showed the cracks: one agent, long lines, crowded pool and locker areas.

b4e6013f8c3f45b1.short: Breakfast let it down, with poor bacon, badly made lobster eggs, stingy portions and pushy bottled-water upsells. Bad enough to cancel Christmas dinner there.

de1b4a772981479d.short: Arrived at 2pm, room not ready until 5:55pm. Told breakfast meant only the $42 continental: one pastry, toast or parfait, coffee or tea, and juice.

e70cfb5fba6132d0.short: The suite award gave a King Bed Suite, and asking guest relations got the corner suite. Strong value at about $800 plus taxes.

15dd1f247136e2ed.short: Flowers, cake, macarons, a stuffed animal and champagne for the son's birthday. Warm stay despite a messy check-in where the desk first claimed no suites.

2d746229e9207b9e.short: Rates far above nearby luxury hotels are hard to justify, and the Intercontinental up the street was more enjoyable. Location is the strong point.

424c7359850a9f9a.short: The standard suite never opened up, so no suite upgrade award. Anniversary cake, juices and a balloon came up to the room.

5f89c542f2a41281.short: The suite is one big room, junior-suite style. Free room service breakfast at any hour, worth about 110 euros, and Chablis on arrival.

83545d2618c17a87.short: No suite free for a 40th anniversary, so the manager arranged a balcony room big enough to pass for a junior suite.

a5cedbd5673f4aaa.short: Bollinger, treats and balloons for the occasion. Still behind true Paris palaces with worn furnishings, and the low 45% occupancy probably explained the upgrade.

dd632ad59e71eb43.short: Family room not ready after 3pm, so a regular room: dated, cramped, A/C struggling in a heatwave. A letdown at a 1,800 EUR rack rate.

ec3255744fae6050.short: Hotel full for two big trade fairs, yet upgraded the day before to a suite never seen in bookable inventory. Terrace food has improved.

f000c9f2e551327a.short: Hairs from the last guest and trash left in the room, still there after telling the desk. Odd smells and daytime construction noise too.

1c3c6a20de8d433b.short: The Park Suite came after a short wait, with a rollaway offered unasked. Cochine bath products, quick housekeeping and a solid breakfast at Opera.

aa8767b3cddcd81f.short: Usually upgraded for free, so spending an award felt like nickel-and-diming. The welcome drink became a massage offer, and new management seems to cut corners.

ac220287bd8fb264.short: A room to rest in at 2pm while the suite was readied. Charming design, lemon cake and macarons, mixed feelings on breakfast, no lounge.

b4a9a1afcdb03f17.short: The pool view was just the other side of the building, understandable on sold-out nights. A bit of a mess: wifi needed manual IP setup.

1168c02ef0d7fff2.short: Newly opened, with a private boutique feel and keen, friendly staff. The one gripe: no proper work desk.

26373c40dc9f2f8c.short: Fruit on arrival, then appetizers and more fruit the second night. The design puts form over function, but it was fun.

5272ededbc0bb3e5.short: Free pickup from the City Air Terminal and subway access were pluses. The suite was somewhat small but fine, and the controls could be confusing.

7d620e430bd7d976.short: About a week with a baby. Quiet river-facing room, and housekeeping cleaned the wood floor for crawling, but the pool was not baby-friendly.

7f42ce922426dbc2.short: Far better than the InterContinental Grand across the street, though the IC's breakfast spread is better. Dinner was good but pricey.

9e4b62e8c8b80594.short: Floor-to-ceiling windows looked over the Olympic Stadium and south Seoul. Breakfast was continental only on day one, fixed the next.

adbce3a1318f4742.short: Weekday breakfast was just pastries and cereal, nothing hot. Ultramodern, and handy for the subway.

bdc264f435eaa84f.short: One of their top Hyatt breakfasts. Sleep suffered from light leaks, motion-sensor bedside panels, thinly insulated plumbing and short sheets.

dabf15e7685ef976.short: Sloppy for a Park Hyatt: a missed cleaning between bookings, ongoing elevator trouble and a remote location. Andaz Seoul next time.

5817c594e4ffd1cc.short: No certificate used. A terrific upgrade, one of the highest-value they have ever had from Hyatt.

64ba3ddd9b91fbdd.short: Asked to move down to a standard room with a Bund view. The hotel insisted the suite was nicer, and the partner preferred it.

a778099431cc23c1.short: No recognition at $3,000 a night, no room until 6pm after a 1pm arrival, cold service in the empty Cloud lounge. Only breakfast was good.

fe0fea160af795aa.short: Taxi greeters, an escort, and a welcome by name at the 87th-floor check-in. Sweeping Shanghai views and a TOTO washlet.

677076154d7ea074.short: Gorgeous, peaceful resort with friendly staff and excellent housekeeping. All four breakfasts were waived, and they'd book again, but only on points.

6d017055e552a0f4.short: Even in quiet late July, a plunge pool suite meant paying $150+ a night. Good family sailing trip and dinner at nearby Spice Mill.

a8c2d6e03379f476.short: Paid $310 a night to move up, skipping a $900-a-night villa. Big suite and plunge pool, but dim lighting and seaweed piled on the beach.

fe532c4a8c3a12e6.short: Going well mid-stay over MLK weekend, with WhatsApp requests answered fast. Breakfast at the Great House, buffet plus an entree, was fully comped.

0d6e9f2d43f260b5.short: The upgrade came after a loyalty concierge put in a good word. Sparkling wine and chocolates, and so far so good despite earlier warnings.

2bc4df598a927b95.short: Passersby could see right in past the low first-floor balconies. The hotel was full, so no chance to move despite the high rate.

6c0b68e756480d3d.short: Nine of about ten stays the prior year got the Deluxe Opera View, but not this one. Maybe a new GM changed the policy.

6e4775277756dd56.short: A modest move since the hotel was full. Damp smell, tiny TV and a cheap bathroom door, and the promised daily amenity never showed.

9c6f89e86a615bd9.short: A weekday stay with the Diamond benefits honored.

a3964f1456155f62.short: Loved the room, service and harbor views. The hotel will not put elites in suites, though, and the value at this price felt doubtful.

b1a9fab64362f069.short: Three categories up, assigned before arrival. Opera House views from the desk, the bed and the soaking tub.

c1b7d6fa75922a17.short: Room ready at 10am, and it felt like a junior suite. One of the best stays of their life, with relaxed, unfussy service.

e5424fed34306fc9.short: Best Hyatt stay ever over five nights. Amazing views, twice-daily housekeeping, a tour of the top-floor Sydney Suite, and Diamonds treated like VIPs.

e94c08c1e8d76e73.short: Room felt small next to other Park Hyatts, though the view and location were good. The made-to-order breakfast dishes disappointed.

02ec5295f0471018.short: Back in the Park Suite several times. Rollaway beds for the kids were free.

052ee772474ffb71.short: Poor AC, a firm bed, furniture that favors looks over comfort, and a lost breakfast order. The suite's design was lovely.

26f4ac6e9407b1e2.short: Booked by his Globalist brother as Guest of Honor. The wine sent up was quickly swapped for sparkling tea, since he doesn't drink.

33ef90111f968127.short: A pleasant stay, and the rollaway bed they asked for was free.

590261c3c384afa3.short: Breakfast in The Bank, the old bank building, came with sparkling wine, and the pool sits in the former vault. Central, excellent staff, highly recommended.

633b274d5be5d80a.short: Spacious, well kept and central, with staff among the best they have met at Park Hyatts. A step up from the Andaz Vienna.

66ca731dce2e5ed5.short: Service beat the Andaz, and the daughter got chocolates. The restaurant crawled on New Year's Eve, and kids' pool hours (11am-6pm) were the main gripe.

8953a24a3bfd149d.short: The single best use of Category 1-7 certificates anywhere, with plans to return. A joking ask for turndown chocolate brought a free box minutes later.

c7f4e32432d1c5b3.short: Excellent dinner at The Bank, with a 7-euro cover for bread. Worth the high cost over the Andaz for a first Vienna visit.

cc8aa6a48cc841b5.short: Good breakfast buffet, especially cook-to-order dishes. The women's sauna runs cooler, so guests use the men's, and a yearly wellness membership costs 2,200 euros.

d7cb83483c5b7312.short: Rollaway quoted at $130 a night, then not charged. Champagne at breakfast, an unbeatable location, better than the Andaz Vienna across the board.

d7e60df019b026cc.short: Gorgeous, with one of the best breakfast buffets they've seen, lots of juices and homemade honeys. Spa and pool beat expectations.

fe3f414952e9baff.short: A November 2021 Christmas markets trip. Breakfast could be room service or The Bank Brasserie buffet, and the concierge sent chocolates.

2267ef6e8c3189af.short: An expiring award confirmed a Park Jr Suite on a $289 rate, and asking for more got the Park Suite. Scuffed molding, worn carpet.

73b388f9042ce978.short: Room not cleaned twice in three nights, though they were out from 11am to mid-afternoon. Guest services oddly asked if cleaning had been requested.

883278773ccd970c.short: Upgraded at check-in even though the hotel was fairly full. Dated but clean, and they would go back at the right rate.

927991eb7da90120.short: Booked through Amex Fine Hotels and Resorts, with a $100 credit and breakfast usable toward Sunday brunch. Blue Duck Tavern's apple pie is a must.

b201da7ef1a9264b.short: Probably their favorite DC stay so far. Staff knew their names by day two, but breakfast is pricey without a benefit.

c849cd9c99512912.short: Suite confirmed by their concierge a few days ahead. Each day's breakfast fit within the $120 credit, and Foggy Bottom was a good base.

cfd38fe51b8e9d37.short: First time back since before the pandemic, and no longer a favorite. Slow valet, no doorman, a so-so gym and dated, worn decor.

de23a051b9912244.short: Upgraded the day before arrival, dog and all, with bowls, water and treats set out. Excellent Blue Duck Tavern food by room service.

e12952da8d5915c1.short: A grand piano and a huge bathroom. The jammed in-room safe took three hours and drills to open, but they would use points here again.

1baaa9284c7fd6b4.short: Kiosk check-in, a small fridge but no microwave. An easy Vegas stop for earning points.

1d9c7911c5d04798.short: Free-night certificates covered the pricey rodeo-weekend nights, and the room was quiet and clean despite a broken safe handle. Mediocre breakfast, great rooftop lounge view.

221359cb5ba5e3b7.short: Pricier breakfast dishes were refused and small juices came instead of large, yet a supervisor said Globalists can order anything. No working heater either.

25cce25d047b2679.short: Roomy, cheap rooms and a big breakfast burrito. The safe was broken the whole visit, even after a report, and the AC was very loud.

28d40834ba882b40.short: Housekeeping dumped clean towels on the counter and left the trash overflowing. Stuffy room, uncomfortable mattress, no desk, but it worked for elite qualifying nights.

29c1c4f9109ed91c.short: Status and elite nights worked fine over several visits. Kiosks kept failing, so even late at night it was the regular check-in line.

3988b9364d6e593a.short: Came back at night to a large cricket on the tissue box. The Globalist breakfast menu at Hash House is limited.

5147383feab6a632.short: The Ipanema tower room was big and nicer than expected off the Strip. Casino smoke, far-off garages and a chaotic weekend breakfast were the downsides.

54fae1a5cd19a15d.short: VIP check-in with no questions asked. Perks favor gamblers, but the renovated rooms make even a quick mattress run worth it.

5fa228205d263831.short: A warning to other Globalists: the French toast came topped with an unpeeled grilled banana, and the waiter claimed that was intentional.

9a3c65966709131e.short: Final bill far below the rate shown when booking through Hyatt, for reasons never looked into. Otherwise as expected, in a good way.

a0b309b1809f1086.short: At an 11am check-in, the kiosk assigned a renovated King, and a manager removed the resort fees. Fantastic value at weekday rates.

acffeaaf551e4516.short: Waited from a 9am arrival rather than take an Ipanema room. The upgrade hit the app around 11am, confirmed at 2:30pm.

c91fc5db0945e635.short: Disliked the connecting layout, with no other renovated room free. Large, clean and comfortable, fine for a cheap Vegas stay but not a special occasion.

cac9b56a6062cb18.short: First a big unrenovated panoramic suite, then a renovated executive suite after asking at VIP check-in. Heavy lobby construction, and breakfast cards covered the tip.

cad3eb1537cb44f5.short: A 4/10 after two stays. Smoke and paint smells, rooms humid even with the AC at 60, a poor off-Strip location, disappointing breakfast.

cfb4d77252a7673e.short: Breakfast felt pared back: some signature items off limits, $7 extra for chicken on a cobb salad, a broken cappuccino machine, and slow, poor service.

f23c9c2c193581c6.short: Big, well-decorated room and handy free valet. Breakfast required the Globalist in person with ID, so a son on a different schedule couldn't go alone.

159cb3066ddb857c.short: The lounge ran oyster and schnitzel nights and knew their drinks by the second evening. Great croissants, and top value for points.

7454be714e3ac7fc.short: Not a fan after nearly a week: sparse rooms, very dark even on sunny days. Bright spots were the bar and fast in-room breakfast.

fb38833eaa321c19.short: Good March 2025 stay, easy subway access, comfy bed, but soupy oatmeal and daily wifi logins. Likely back to the cheaper Gild Hall next time.

246cfd87d5d7d9eb.short: Untrained housekeeping and key readers that failed after hours, the weekend after reopening. Valet was covered on points, and Sporting Club access was a plus.

5a676a38f25d4671.short: Terrific Sporting Club, handy Broad Street location, though the nearby Centric edges it on rooms. One free drink at Pergola, where construction blocks the view.

6a78642fdcb0a693.short: Huge but worn room, noisy through connected air vents and from the street. Sporting Club closed and rates high, so a return is doubtful.

b7707f2aa63add1b.short: Mediocre at best, with a room that never cooled below 71 and noise even in interior rooms. No plans to stay again.

b9f36f3f3d2d2482.short: Well-finished rooms and an impressive Sporting Club, but lots of street noise. The 19th-floor buffet is free for Globalists, poor value for anyone paying.

bb9f9de32155d52d.short: A Bellevue Suite was offered only as a $50 a night upsell, poor value against the certificate. The Avenue Suite faced the atrium, rather gloomy.

f5bbbaf5ec173ea7.short: Renovation felt about 75% done, and the $42 breakfast ran light. Room size and the Sporting Club still beat the nearby Centric for leisure.

04bb682a3801c538.short: Fantastic room, and street noise was no issue up top. Better food at the Hyatt Regency Austin midweek, but the Driskill wins on character.

2908ce8344de8ac4.short: The tiniest suite ever seen, and regular rooms are very small too. Would never stay again: the Hyatt Regency gave free suite upgrades.

5b38d86b0875b8e6.short: The suite would not heat to 69 degrees and maintenance could not fix it on a Saturday night. Probably the Hyatt Regency next time.

5ffaaaf153077032.short: Check-in at 1:30pm, a 2pm checkout offer, and birthday beers and cake for their brother. One of the best US stays despite patchy wifi.

82b06296982d1f45.short: One of the worst rooms in 20 years, at nearly $400 a night during ACL. An hour-plus at the desk got a decent one.

9182f3d513b10d55.short: Valet never hit the bill, and the $100 daily breakfast credit at 1886 Cafe worked well. But street noise, a crooked bathroom door, slow drains.

cf027f0165066f03.short: The larger room was not as small as feared, and the Travel Leaders package included a food-and-beverage credit. Decent service, historic feel, good location.

f950e1afc070522d.short: Small windows in the living room and bedroom face another building. Limited light, but not so you'd notice.

ff96cc06ab0fa132.short: Used an expiring award for a junior suite despite warnings it was not worth it, and got a Landmark Suite instead. Superb.

577a8c07319bf1b4.short: Two breakfast vouchers a day: the set Elite Breakfast or $15 toward the menu. Free shave ice, fast valet, a tiny pool fine for kids.

6d98beb8804667ad.short: Asked twice for a suite, none available. Breakfast choice: Japanese set at Mizuki, Western buffet at La Locanda, or room service.

98bb7dd6364921bf.short: Sunrise side as requested, then a beach villa for the last night. Good villas, but dining and butler service were inconsistent.

2d335ee71b3dce6d.short: Train noise was audible but didn't disrupt sleep. Strong shower, comfy bed, 4pm checkout offered, and breakfast at etta Cafe ran under $20.

ad53bcde934de70e.short: Pastries, drinks and $11 juices on top of entrees, well over $100 a day, and never billed a cent. Cafe staff bent over backwards.

b64f46901a5aa092.short: The suite upgrade looked more like a King Studio, but they were out most of the time. Still a great stay, with gorgeous finishes.

e6d376a963204788.short: Upgraded the same day. Service still felt tentative in the soft opening and the cashless setup made tipping awkward, but staff were good overall.

eb5bf0cea4150f08.short: Poor soundproofing: road and truck noise from 6am, footsteps above, heavy doors with no soft-close. Breakfast looked to cover $25 a person, food only.

da9d1dde56e97e5e.short: Great housekeeping, a refurbished spa and sunset views at the bar, but a little tired now, with worn carpets and pool deck and slower service.

ac4f885732f72e19.short: Nightly Upgrade Awards were pulled two days out, but the beachside plunge-pool villa came free anyway. Outstanding service, disappointing food and grounds.

68f0124b6f0ea7ea.short: Storm-damaged boardwalk and private docks, a north-facing overwater villa turned down as a downgrade, and no answer about paid upgrades. Otherwise near perfect.

c1666631746d382e.short: Plenty of room for two kids, but a bathroom without privacy. Smooth seaplane, excellent snorkeling off the deck, great meals at Crust and Alba.

f453482a09efd70a.short: A 20-minute check-in wait, and the Executive King looked like the base room, maybe higher up. Recommended, but not the flawless St. Regis expected.

63e3097eff08738c.short: Dull renovation, a shower that sprayed across the bathroom, atrociously slow internet and a subpar breakfast with no coffee refills. Close to Times Square.

de4330e9148bdf49.short: A daily resort fee plus paid beach chairs and umbrellas, pools too small when full, scarce parking and heavy timeshare pitches. Prefers the nearby Sheraton.

54a0ef29e13e56ca.short: Four Nightly Upgrade Awards turned the cheapest room into a suite going for over $1,000 a night. Almost no construction noise.

5142dba9d5df981a.short: Suites showed as available, yet the desk's 'nice high floor corner room' was a standard 12th-floor room. Free parking and a 4pm checkout.

bc358790115afcdd.short: Booked the day before. Modern with brutalist touches, floor-to-ceiling windows and a huge shower, but hallway noise and Saturday 6th Street parties carried in.

481328e0fabb7666.short: Upgraded in the app minutes after booking, then extended a night. Room-service breakfast was very good and fully wiped off the bill.

d0e97be2c77ac35b.short: Much better than a regular room, mostly for the bigger shower. Quick, tasty room-service breakfast on real plates.

f0c4747277f86aec.short: The higher floor was pitched as an upgrade, but the view was identical. Fridge not cold, poor noise isolation, good location.

ba2be29b700f94bf.short: Pre-upgraded in the app, then no recognition at check-in. Desk staff seemed very new, and minibar access became a multi-hour saga.

d3d347cb246b519d.short: Globalist room service breakfast from 6:30am, with a $35-a-person allowance. One order arrived with errors after a 7am confirmation call, and the next was flawless.

69635d473063daaf.short: Every suite type showed open in the app, though none was requested. Small room, weak water pressure, and the breakfast tip hit the folio.

170e7e89792003d7.short: Bumped from the Skyline Suite to the Mile High Suite the day before. Fabulous tub, but street and social-club noise reached the 11th floor.

494cda578e299f2b.short: Great breakfast at Chez Maggy, where the Globalist allowance is reportedly up to $80, though the pre-arrival email listed $35 per person.

9efcb93959b704d9.short: Texted en route about a King Balcony, then offered an Executive Suite ready later that day. Breakfast was outstanding: chilaquiles on a hash-brown base.

cca2bb0a4ff391f1.short: The suite had no door between bedroom and living area. Breakfast for four, quoted at an absurd $60, was wiped at checkout.

77fe8b1829fb871a.short: Fantastic, with a plush bed and linens, good shower pressure, pretty marble and wood. Wine and ham at check-in, chocolates in the room, 4pm checkout.

88cccfe4e0689ef3.short: Upgraded before arrival, then white wine and ham tapas in the lobby. Nice rooms, incredibly hard beds, and no connecting rooms here.

a1aa0988f51bf9e2.short: OMAR breakfast included an entree and dessert: try the egg and waffles and the churro with chocolate. Warm staff, modest welcome gift.

8b668d5ff94aa467.short: Comped valet ($45 a night) and happy hour, plus a $60 daily breakfast credit even for one person. Decor and Marsh House impressed.

239188fff4e0ed33.short: Separate FHR bookings were combined at check-in. About $100 of breakfast wiped each morning, resort fees removed on request, so only parking was paid.

32770da012caa8f9.short: Liked it a lot. Big bathroom, a sparsely furnished terrace, a poor work setup, and traffic noise from Indian Canyon Drive.

34ef7125756cbd8f.short: Breakfast and the amenity fee never hit the bill, and the premium internet charge came off. Few suites, so suite upgrades are likely rare.

250055f8410be9c2.short: A generous upgrade for six nights, a 750mL Cabernet and very good breakfast at Landrace. Probably won't book elsewhere on future San Antonio trips.

72feabe3fa52b193.short: Told no suites were available, though the app showed some. Valet (over $40 a day) was covered, rooftop breakfast capped at $25 a person daily.

b3c1766f1b135c5e.short: Very attractive room: wood floors, a latticed shower door, container ships passing on the river. The firm mattress was great thanks to amazingly soft linens.

1f11798ffe5f111b.short: Asking about suites got only a paid upgrade offer at a Globalist discount. Otherwise fine: Puget Sound views, champagne and 4pm checkout.

210776ee2e40bccc.short: Unprofessional front desk, with no Globalist acknowledgment, just benefit printouts. Dinner charges were wiped but in-room breakfast was not, though breakfast itself was great.

45c671139f05f430.short: Soft lighting and lovely design for $121 a night, but an extremely small desk. Breakfast came by delivery, and the destination fee came off automatically.

edc34506cd9010f8.short: Underwhelming. No coffee, water or phone in the room, a cleaning rag in the closet, and water only after asking at the desk.

6c450dc98319ba50.short: Clean room, fast wifi, well-meaning service short on polish and follow-through. The suites are really junior suites, and beach rooms have zero privacy.

fb9883d7b5f99760.short: Dark, depressing lower-floor suite, then a move upstairs after asking: bigger patio, smaller room. The gym was in a dingy temporary space.

1dac5ef7f604b4aa.short: Moved up after contacting the hotel before arrival, without spending any Nightly Upgrade Awards. Welcome drinks at check-in.

b52c9152af9e32d8.short: Texts from the W Insider while the room was readied, wine and chocolates, room breakfast with no bill. Late checkout only to noon.

1425e40da3707dc7.short: A lei, a welcome drink and a drink voucher. Clean, with good staff and an adults-only infinity pool, but pricey at cash rates.

a5a91642cb75bd78.short: Used a breakfast voucher at the on-site Starbucks. No suite, but a great stay.

a8dc90f325edc52d.short: Awards cleared to an Alcove family suite five days out, then the Grand Suite at arrival. Hot breakfast items cost $6 to $8 extra.

b92cb55cc3802a28.short: Excellent value and a spacious room, but VIP check-in took over 30 minutes and vegan breakfast meant just potatoes and fruit. Would return.

4f0f38292dbb9d8b.short: 4pm checkout on request, free parking and a VIP desk that knew the perks. The pool was closed and Masquerade Tower felt dated.

0d66f8a83f6ddabd.short: Base rooms ran over $400 a night. Great suite with views of Seoul, one more impressive Hyatt on this Asia trip.

9a439d923557695b.short: Pancakes and an omelet came in under three minutes, and the roughly $50 bill was taken off automatically. Would return in a heartbeat.

52e8b125f783e0aa.short: Only the bedroom has windows, so the living room gets little daylight. Spacious, quiet, and one block from Michigan Avenue.

58c36cca7169cab5.short: Quiet, comfortable room despite a dated tub and shower curtain. Breakfast was not included, and the buffet cost $32 a person plus tax.

470b7c5b561fc87d.short: Upgrade confirmed by email within a couple of days of booking, and the desk set up 4pm checkout unasked. Would absolutely return.

aa204467d5cbbf66.short: Confirmed a Park Suite, got the larger Georgetown Suite. After an overcharge, each day's breakfast bill was wiped, nearly $200 the first morning.

79466b1a9cb7bba5.short: Breakfast covered one main plus hot and cold drinks, and a dirty martini setup was the welcome gift. Good hotel, no wow factor.

5f83bd33abe895d6.short: No suites for any Globalist in house, unlike before the renovation, when they almost always got one. Scratchy towels, but would gladly return.

2fe5bb4c9cb89966.short: Welcome cookies came late but hot, and a second bag waited at checkout. Bridal suite with a balcony and ceilings at least 12 feet high.

a993290c5cfe2fcb.short: A breakfast of about $50 was credited in full despite a $20 cap. Practically flawless, even with $55 nightly valet and slow Wi-Fi.

eca5e92c159315e2.short: A 25th anniversary stay with champagne and chocolate-covered strawberries waiting. Very high cash rates, even for New York, but would definitely return.

d5ff53b170f1faa9.short: A fumbled check-in, with the name taken twice and the reservation not found at first. Massive, gorgeous rooms, though holiday service was off.

dd961adf78beba7e.short: The upgrade wasn't needed: only about 100 square feet more, a balcony facing a parking lot, and no vineyard views or outdoor soaking tub.

45ca392ea92e8515.short: Mentioning a major anniversary brought a bottle of the resort's own Swing Pinot Noir. Excellent but pricey dining, and falconry at $135 a person.

25242671992843d8.short: 1970s-style brown-and-orange decor and a shallow sink that splashes the wallpaper every time. Fine, but not worth going out of the way for.

87d52313307d96f0.short: The parlor suite was two connecting rooms, one with a sofa bed. Lounge still closed and no room service, but the staff were all friendly.

a513fa72226e7bdb.short: Sold out, so no suite. Breakfast was covered for her mother's separate room too, and a CA$5 tip charge was quickly reversed.

059137c2543e0dcd.short: Excellent value, with standard rooms at about $110 to $150 a night. A Thai outfit and a handwritten card were left for their daughter.

00b3be16c8108e33.short: Chose to wait until 4pm for the suite the app had shown. The water never got hot either night, and the coffee was weak.

831cd86f2d17bf7a.short: The $100 credit covered almost all of a Pergola dinner. The 100,000 sq ft Sporting Club alone made it worthwhile.

cea5562a88107f7f.short: Two days without water, and no warning of the second outage even though staff knew. Already booked to return next February.

69060163773eb6fd.short: Anniversary champagne and a note from the GM were waiting. Late checkout meant a day room until 4pm, as the suite wasn't free past 11am.

c3ed8e28fa212034.short: Floaties for the boys and wine with a personal note were waiting. For a family, the savings and recognition made the status worth earning.

54c906fbfef3d759.short: Free minibar, and free wine and sake at happy hour. A 2,200 yen per-person Rooftop Bar cover only showed up on the checkout bill.

63ed275c68521146.short: Like a small apartment, with a full kitchen and washer-dryer, but little view. Excellent value on points, with cash around $580 a night.

e6be2c17ca0ae0a2.short: Chosen over the Hyatt Regency Tokyo for the Shibuya location. Spotless room with a kitchenette and a washer-dryer that ran about four hours.

71e7f5775a1a3b38.short: Best food yet at an all-inclusive, especially the Cielo rooftop. The beach was a letdown, with kelp and persistent vendors, but no hesitation about returning.

3e96fb0757ad81b1.short: A 463 sq ft room with Salvatore Ferragamo toiletries and an excellent ocean view from the small balcony. Near the top of his all-inclusive list.

3fe7a76789b0172c.short: Daily schedules and balloons for the kids came from butler Andre. Worth every point, even after a Louisiana hurricane nearly made them cancel.

bfa89fd4a9aa9231.short: Emailed ahead about the birthday and found a gift and letter waiting. Best booked on points, with cash often over $400 before taxes.

56f1853e4e845e7f.short: The Globalist gift was just a small Kuromoji pillow mist. Breakfast is now in the club, no longer the full Crossroads Kitchen buffet.

adb89e9f1a646d71.short: Service ranged from excellent concierge help to cold, and the pool was underwhelming. Reclassified as a resort on April 1, so no guaranteed 4pm checkout.

b4f6dec055cffe88.short: Mount Fuji showed from the west-facing suite one clear morning. Leaving was bittersweet, despite a leaking shower and a concierge booking never followed up.

928b83d38cf9524c.short: Ruinart Blanc de Blancs and butter cookies for the birthday. The bed was firm, bar service lacking, and value doubtful next to the Andaz Tokyo.

d04ca40d77ee76a2.short: A stopover on points, with cash about $650 a night. The room was huge by Tokyo standards, and breakfast excellent apart from slightly underdone eggs.

4d0f142f7e5f724b.short: The award confirmed a Grand Executive Suite, then check-in brought the Diplomat Suite. Keeping it meant checkout at 1pm, not 4pm.

84b770d8ef38f5a8.short: A rollaway and couch bedding were ready in advance, and the club's evening spread could pass for dinner. Would absolutely return.

e8039a665527c796.short: Paid $560++ a night extra for the water villa, and the New Year's Eve gala was a mandatory $510 per person. A very special island.

438965c85ab6fd99.short: The ocean view came despite a warning that peak-season upgrades were limited. The resort was full but never felt crowded, and they'd happily return.

957b02f66068789e.short: Gigantic suite with its own gym and a jacuzzi tub, though a semi-public path runs past the patio. Strongly recommended.

c3af7e6625264959.short: A massive but worn suite, with tired cushions, thin towels and a disappointing patio view. Surprisingly great food, but the rooms desperately need renovating.

a602aac1043e7f6b.short: Large balcony over the waves and El Arco, sofa made into a king bed nightly. Beach not swimmable, but she wants to return with friends.

ec9c2d414af64e24.short: A deal of a lifetime next to the roughly $3,700 nightly cash rate, with tequila and a fruit plate on arrival.

f74cbe2c759b60ef.short: The nicest Hyatt Place yet, steps from Marutamachi Station. Breakfast had salmon, miso and eggs to order, about $17 a person without Globalist status.

a5733c5d2355218b.short: Left-behind bathroom items were cataloged and shipped free to the next hotel, 250 miles away, arriving two days later. Breakfast had make-your-own sushi.

bd52bcce38b26204.short: A top-five room ever, but bags with medication and a laptop went missing until a third follow-up. Just one fish seen in the lagoon.

d825ed15356d3549.short: Small room, little view, thin amenities for the price, and no hurry back despite friendly staff. The $35 daily destination fee was never charged.

a5eb62fbe05d3fec.short: The $50 Prive credit nearly covered a $52 dinner. A large open-plan suite with a wet bar and soaking tub, highly recommended.

a3db6a5ace054f2d.short: Spectacular value for a suite that retailed for about $1,160 a night. Possibly the best club lounge at any Hyatt so far, with free-flowing Ruinart.

f925d8a92d68eff6.short: Excellent club lounge and magnificent harbor views, though the rooms look aged. Corporate rates booked direct need proof of eligibility here.
